description: The approval code of a pairing on Linux (ADR 0164): six decimal digits that the pairing device shows and the person types at the computer. The device shows them in two groups of three (`482 913`) and the computer reads what the person typed as follows: only the ASCII digits 0 to 9 and the ASCII space count, blanks may stand anywhere and are ignored, and exactly six digits must remain. Any other character (a letter, a tab, a line break, a hyphen, a full-width or an Arabic-Indic digit, a combining mark) makes the whole text not a code. `digits` is the six digits that remain, or null; `grouped` is how a device shows a code that was read (three digits, one space, three digits). The Rust protocol crate passes the `digits` of every case; the clients that show a code pass the `grouped` ones.

cases.name: a line break after the digits
a combining mark after the sixth digit
